$comment: Single source of truth for presets. Read by TypeScript (src/presets) and by
Python (tools/generate_precomputed.py), so a preset cannot be defined in the
app in a form Python never validated.
Naming follows the package's rule: a value ending in _age is an AGE (years
before present), one ending in _date is a DATE (years after Day 1 of
Creation). Chronology fields are DATEs except age_of_earth.
PROVISIONAL: the septuagint chronology values are placeholders chosen to
exercise a longer timeline. They are on the pre-publication checklist in
frontend_plan.md and must be reviewed, with a citation, before this ships.

septuagint.label: Septuagint (LXX)
septuagint.note: PROVISIONAL — placeholder values pending review and citation.

pc_c.label: Precambrian-Cambrian
pc_c.note: 540 Ma; the boundary the package's own run config fits.

second_constraint.label: End of the Ice Age
second_constraint.note: Held across every preset; its AGE comes from the chronology.

defaults.$comment: Precambrian-Cambrian by default: it is the only boundary whose calibration reaches the whole geologic column, and it is the configuration the package's own run config and the paper's headline result use. Pinning the Flood to a younger boundary caps the oldest apparent age the model can produce, which is correct but makes the column chart open half empty.

general.label: Creation week + Flood
note: Authored but not exposed in v1. Turning this on is flipping `enabled`;
no component changes, because the parameter panel iterates the free
names Python returns rather than a hardcoded list.
Freeing lambda_c/k_c does not disturb the calibration: both constraint
ages map to formation DATEs at or after t_F, so their integrals cover
only the Flood and post-Flood regions and the Creation-week parameters
never enter. Verified to exactly zero difference.
